hypothesis: Maintaining 227 distinct words and allowing descendant conflicts can cross barriers unavailable to feasible local repair.
method: Tabu single-word replacement; bit flips, relocations, random replacements and periodic global word scans.
prediction: Reach at least one low-conflict state structurally far from the 226-word parent within 90 CPU seconds; target cost zero.
falsification: No low-conflict states outside parent basin; higher evaluation throughput without structural diversity does not support the hypothesis.

hypothesis: Large ejections, cross-weight destruction and acceptance of smaller feasible packings can escape the restricted repairs already exhausted.
method: Greedy refill after random, weight-band or forced-outsider destroy; accept neutral and probabilistically worse states; return to incumbent after stagnation.
prediction: Generate structurally distinct 220+ packings and eventually >=227.
falsification: Repeatedly rebuild the same parent or spend the budget below 220 without useful diversity.

hypothesis: Persistent penalties on recurring received-word collisions can move the 227-word packing out of a two-collision basin; bounded excursions preserve proximity without erasing learned penalties.
prediction: Within 300 seconds, lower unweighted cost below 2 or preserve near-valid states farther than 16 words from the parent.
falsification: Only repeated returns to the same two-collision basin or no penalty updates; higher evaluation count is not progress.
earlier_implementation_failure: A restart reset the stagnation timer before it triggered weight updates; corrected by global-iteration scheduling and explicit update counters.

hypothesis: Recombining multiple strong packings can cross a barrier requiring many simultaneous cross-weight replacements.
method: Exact pair-union independent sets by matching, then CP-SAT for four-way unions with graph clique cuts.
prediction: At least one pair yields 227, or four-way unions expose additional choices beyond every pair optimum.
falsification: Exact pair-union bounds all <=226; four-way INFEASIBLE rules out only that named finite union.

hypothesis: A collection of outsiders each blocked by only 2-3 parent words can form a profitable large exchange even when every small weight-window repair fails.
method: CP-SAT over all original parent words plus every outsider with <=k distinct parent blockers; no bound on number removed, clique cuts from the conflict graph.
prediction: k=2 or k=3 yields a larger packing or a compact exact exclusion; do not confuse k with exchange radius.
falsification: INFEASIBLE at target 227 certifies exclusion within this whole candidate pool, not globally.
